A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original jailbreak-defense experiments, general-ability evaluations, over-refusal analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds defense comparisons, evaluations on additional model configurations, and a response-length analysis.

M1.justification: SwaRD, safety pivot tokens, guardrail-assisted tagging, and the CPO objective remain unchanged. R2D-ZeroThink becomes R2D-n with the same described inference behavior. Clarifying that training targets contain pivot tokens does not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca and AdvBench for training, JailbreakBench and HarmBench for jailbreak evaluation, XSTest, and the same general-ability benchmarks. Additional model configurations and harmful-versus-benign length comparisons retain existing task coverage. Multi-turn attacks appear only as future work.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates RPO, Self-Reminder, and IA against R2D across PAIR, GCG, and JBC on four models. These methods were discussed or cited in v2 but lacked reported comparative results. The original Table 1 comparator set remains, substantially broadening the evaluated defense comparisons.

E3.justification: General-ability evaluation expands from one to six non-reasoning model configurations, and component ablations extend to three reasoning models. Figure 5 introduces a harmful-versus-benign comparison using generated word counts as a latency proxy. Existing datasets, judges, metrics, sample counts, and training settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends CPO and pivot-removal ablations from four non-reasoning models to include R1-7B, R1-32B, and QwQ-32B, testing component contributions in models that already reason. New Figure 5 examines query-dependent generation length. Appendix cases and the Dic-Judge analysis are retained; the latter moves into Figure 4b.

E5.justification: The response-length values with ± reporting remain unchanged in v2 Table 3 and v3 Table 2. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the additions introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and Figure 5 add substantial general-ability, ablation, comparator, and response-length results. Figure 3 also changes existing HarmBench values: PAIR on Vicuna-13B changes from 47%/21% original/R2D ASR to 21%/21%, under unchanged reported settings. The stated maximum pivot-removal increase changes from 33% to 45%, correcting the prose to match a difference already present in v2 Table 4. Retained general-ability scores are otherwise equivalently rounded.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same dataset construction, distillation objective, probability decomposition, CPO loss, and ASR formula. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: safety-aware reasoning through SwaRD and CPO improves jailbreak defense while preserving general capabilities and avoiding over-refusal. Added experiments support existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 attributes longer harmful-query responses to safety checks and rethinking, adds interpretations of comparisons with contemporary defenses, and identifies multi-turn defense as future work. Some new interpretations need qualification: word counts do not directly measure latency, and Table 5 includes exceptions to superiority, such as Mistral PAIR ASR of 11% for R2D versus 8% for IA.

D1.justification: The Ethics Statement newly declares datasets, alongside code, publicly available; v2 already provided the code link. Appendix training settings, hardware, synthesis instructions, and evaluation tools remain unchanged. Conversely, v3 removes explicit explanations that the CPO ablation uses only SwaRD and that pivot removal also excludes CPO, reducing recipe clarity.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Crescendo and Tang et al.'s multi-turn attack work in the limitations discussion. It also develops empirical positioning against the already-cited RPO, Self-Reminder, and IA. The related-work sections and central novelty positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 expands the Section 3 heading, renames R2D-ZeroThink to R2D-n, shortens the ablation discussion, and incorporates Appendix A.3's discussion into the main text. It also edits the abstract, affiliations, and acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from four small vertical charts to a larger 2×2 horizontal arrangement with common axis limits. The two existing over-refusal plots are combined as Figure 4a–b. A new latency-proxy figure and defense table are added, the ablation table becomes full-width, and the expanded general-ability table becomes a compact single-column display.

improvement.justification: The added contemporary defenses and broader utility and component evaluations address gaps in v2's support for its safety and capability-preservation claims. These provide a meaningful but limited quality gain. Reduced ablation-recipe clarity, sparse details for the added analyses, and latency and superiority interpretations that require qualification constrain the improvement.
